 THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 08.04.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA NO. 2191 OF 2013 3  2025:KER:32958  JUDGMENT Dated this the 8th day of April, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No. 701/2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pala, is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.04.2010.

According to the petitioner, on 12.04.2010 at about 7.55 a.m., while he was walking along the side of the road, a bus bearing Reg.No. KA-19/AC/5577 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, ran over her right foot and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3.
The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
is Rs.12,96,000/-(limited to Rs.8,00,000/-).
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the 2025:KER:32958 accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A13, B1 and X1.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs. 1,17,586/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.

sentences.text: 7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri. Thomas Abraham, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.A.R.George, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.

According to him, the petitioner was a B.Sc.
Nursing 2025:KER:32958 student.

The Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.1,500/-.
11.
At the time of the accident, the petitioner was a 3rd year B.Sc Nursing student at Sahyadri College of Nursing, Mangalore.
Ext. A9
certificate issued from Sahyadri College of Nursing, states that she was a 2nd year B.Sc Nursing student in the said college in 2009.
Ext.A12 is the fee structure of the B.Sc. Nursing course, stating that the fee for a year comes to Rs. 60,000/- and the hostel fee is Rs. 15,000/-.

The Tribunal has fixed the notional income of the petitioner as Rs. 1500/-.
12.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2010 will come to Rs.7500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that she is a B.Sc. Nursing Student, her notional income is to be fixed much above that of a coolie.

13. In the decision in K.P.Joyappan v. Mathai T.V. and others, (M.A.C.A.No. 2188 of 2015), this Court has fixed the notional income of a B.Sc Nursing Student involved in an accident in the year 2013, at Rs. 12,500/-.

entities.text: K.P.Joyappan v. Mathai T.V. and others, (M.A.C.A.No. 2188 of 2015)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the decision in Liss J. Purakari v. The Manager, The New India Assurance Co. Lrd (M.A.C.A.No. 130 of 2014), the notional income 2025:KER:32958 of a B.com student involved in an accident in the year 2010 was fixed by this Court at Rs.11,000/-.

entities.text: Liss J. Purakari v. The Manager, The New India Assurance Co. Lrd (M.A.C.A.No. 130 of 2014)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the fact that, in this case, the accident occurred in the year 2010, the notional income of the petitioner is fixed at Rs. 11,000/-.

14. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
1. Dorsal composite loss (R) foot.
2. Extended tenderness losses L.T And multiple abrasion.
15. Ext. X1 disability certificate shows that the petitioner suffered 14.19% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by the medical board.

The Tribunal, however, scaled down the percentage of Riya Merin Varghese vs The Oriental Insurance Company Limited on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84198193/
3 disability of the petitioner to 8%.

sentences.text: When the petitioner was examined as PW1, she deposed that because of the injuries sustained in the accident, she had to discontinue her B.Sc Nursing course and thereafter she had to confine herself as a home maker.
The fact that, because of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner discontinued her B.Sc. Nursing course is not under challenge.
In the above circumstances, the functional disability of the petitioner is much more than the permanent physical disability assessed as per Ext.A1.
Since because of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner lost her entire career, her functional disability is fixed at 40%.
16. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 20 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.13,30,560/-.
17. Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.4500/- being the income for 3 months @ Rs.1500/-.
Because of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, she had to discontinue her B.Sc. Nursing course and had to lead the life of a home maker.

From Ext.A12 fee structure of the B.Sc. Nursing course, it is revealed that the annual fee was Rs.
60,000/- and the hostel fee was Rs. 15,000/-.
She had to discontinue the study while she was in the 2 nd year.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to get reasonable compensation towards 'loss of study'.
Considering the facts, towards loss of study, a consolidated sum of Rs.100000/- is awarded.
18. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.18,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs. 3,000/- was awarded, towards extra nourishment Rs.1000/- was awarded and towards 2025:KER:32958 'bystander expenses' Rs. 3,200/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
19. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 18 days in two spells.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life', extra nourishment and 'bystander expenses' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.75,000/-,1,00,000/-,
4000/- and 36,00/- (200x 18 days) respectively.
20.
Towards 'transportation' the Tribunal was awarded a sum of Rs. 7,000/-.
but the petitioner claimed a sum of Rs. 18,000/-.
She also produced receipts in that respect.
Therefore, she is entitled to get a sum of Rs. 18,000/- towards transportation expenses.
21. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

22. In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.16,87,566/-, (Rupees sixteen lakhs eighty seven thousand five hundred and sixty six only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation,
excluding interest for a period of 109 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal,
with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
24. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse 2025:KER:32958 the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.

25. The Tribunal found that the 1st respondent had no valid driving licence at the time of the accident and therefore, the 3rd respondent was permitted to recover the compensation from the 1st respondent.
During the pendency of the appeal, the 1st respondent had produced his valid driving licence.
The same was verified by the learned Standing Counsel and admitted that, the 1st respondent had valid driving licence at the time of the accident.
Therefore the permission granted to the 3rd respondent to recover the compensation from the 1st respondent is set aside.
